sentence_stem: If I had more free time,
correct_completion: I would learn to play the guitar.
full_sentence: If I had more free time, I would learn to play the guitar.
acceptable_variants: I would take a music class.

options.text: I will learn to play the guitar next year.
options.why_wrong: This is a real plan for the future. The stem sets up an imagined situation, which needs a second conditional result.

options.text: I learned to play the guitar when I was young.
options.why_wrong: This describes a past event, which does not follow from the hypothetical condition in the stem.

options.text: I would learn to play the guitar.
I have learned to play the guitar already.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect describes a finished experience, not an imagined result of a condition.

grammar_focus: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb
explanation: The second conditional describes an unreal or unlikely situation in the present and its imagined result. The if-clause uses the past simple, and the main clause uses would plus the base verb. Spanish speakers often place the conditional form in the if-clause, which is a common mistake in English.
translation: Si tuviera más tiempo libre, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.
